hooks.text: President Bill Clinton went on television to announce a rock from Mars.
Did a four-pound Antarctic rock actually carry fossilized life from Mars?
A four-pound Martian meteorite sat in Antarctica for thirteen thousand years.

title: The President's Martian Rock
description: Discover how a four-pound meteorite found in Antarctica sparked a global debate and a presidential address about life on Mars.

beats.text: President Bill Clinton went on television to announce a rock from Mars.
beats.visual: photograph of President Bill Clinton delivering his 1996 meteorite speech, White House, 1996

beats.text: In December 1984, meteorite hunters exploring the Allan Hills region of Antarctica discovered an unusual four-pound specimen.
beats.visual: photograph of the Allan Hills icefield in Antarctica, ANSMET field team, 1984

beats.text: A colossal asteroid impact had blasted this ancient stone off the Martian surface around sixteen million years ago.
beats.visual: artist's concept of a large asteroid hitting the Martian surface, 2020

beats.text: After drifting through the freezing vacuum of the solar system, the meteorite finally landed on Earth approximately thirteen thousand years ago.
beats.visual: diagram of a meteorite's interplanetary transit path from Mars to Earth, 2020

beats.text: In 1996, NASA scientists announced the specimen contained microscopic structures measuring twenty to one hundred nanometers in diameter.
beats.visual: scanning electron microscope image of ALH 84001 microscopic structures, NASA, 1996

beats.text: Though most researchers eventually rejected a biological origin, this remarkable Martian rock inspired that historic television address by the President.
beats.visual: photograph of the ALH 84001 meteorite specimen, NASA Johnson Space Center, 1996
